question.text: An Indian importer needs to pay USD 50,000 in 2 months. How many lots of USDINR futures should they buy to hedge?

explanation.text: The Logic: The USDINR lot size is 1,000 USD (p. 51), and an importer can go long USDINR futures to hedge a dollar payable (p. 119). USD 50,000 / 1,000 = 50 lots. The Trap: The lot size is 1,000 USD, not 10,000 or 100. Misreading the lot size produces an order of magnitude error. Note: If the exposure does not divide evenly by the lot size, the hedge will be imperfect; the workbook explicitly notes over-hedging or under-hedging in that situation (p. 125).
